creator: Alexander Terp
description:
In a pane on the owner's laptop (0.19.0, 2026-10-27), `which ghostty` prints `/Applications/Muster.app/Contents/Library/MusterSessions.app/Contents/Resources/muster-daemon-data/bin/ghostty`. That is `packaging/muster-daemon-data/bin/ghostty`, Muster's stand-in for Ghostty's `+ssh` helper, not Ghostty. Anything but `ghostty +ssh` goes to a real `ghostty` further along the PATH, and when there is none the stand-in prints "no Ghostty is installed" and exits 64.

The laptop has no real one on the PATH even though `/Applications/Ghostty.app` (Homebrew cask, 1.3.1) is installed, because the cask links no `ghostty` command into `/opt/homebrew/bin`. So `ghostty --version` in a pane there reports that Ghostty is not installed, which is false.

The stand-in does not need to be on the PATH at all. Ghostty's shell integration calls it by absolute path, `"$GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR/ghostty" +ssh` (zsh `ghostty-integration`, bash `ghostty.bash`). It is on the PATH only because the daemon turns on the integration's `path` feature (`spawn.rs`), which appends `$GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`, and that is how `bin/muster` reaches panes whose profile set PATH outright. The stand-in's forward-to-a-real-ghostty loop exists only because of that.

Open: move `bin/muster` to a directory of its own that the daemon appends itself, leaving the stand-in reachable only through `$GHOSTTY_BIN_DIR`, and drop the forwarding loop. Or keep the layout and have the stand-in also try `/Applications/Ghostty.app/Contents/MacOS/ghostty` on macOS, with a message that says it found no `ghostty` on the PATH rather than that none is installed.
title: A pane's `ghostty` is Muster's ssh stand-in, which says Ghostty is not installed when it is
